issue_title: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fileno' on reconnection with worker_cancel_long_running_tasks_on_connection_loss

(if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery version affected). - [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery. - [x] I have included the contents of ``pip freeze`` in the issue. - [x] I have included all the versions of all the external dependencies required to reproduce this bug. ## Optional Debugging Information - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one Python version and/or implementation. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one message broker and/or result backend. - [x] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one version of the message broker and/or result backend. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one operating system. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one workers pool. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue with autoscaling, retries, ETA/Countdown & rate limits disabled. - [x] I have tried reproducing the issue after downgrading and/or upgrading Celery and its dependencies. ## Related Issues and Possible Duplicates #### Related Issues - None #### Possible Duplicates - None ## Environment & Settings **Celery version**:

### Other Dependencies

celery_config.py ```python task_acks_late = True broker_connection_retry_on_startup = True broker_channel_error_retry = True broker_connection_max_retries = None worker_cancel_long_running_tasks_on_connection_loss = True ``` rabbitmq.conf ``` consumer_timeout = 61000 ```

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

celery_config.py ```python task_acks_late = True broker_connection_retry_on_startup = True broker_channel_error_retry = True broker_connection_max_retries = None worker_cancel_long_running_tasks_on_connection_loss = True ``` rabbitmq.conf ``` consumer_timeout = 61000 ``` celery.py ```python from celery import Celery app = Celery('src', broker='amqp://guest@localhost//', include=['src.tasks']) app.config_from_object('celery_config') ``` tasks.py ```python from src.celery import app import time @app.task def timeout_rabbitmq(): print('RabbitMQ timeout task') time.sleep(70) return ``` run.py ```python from src.tasks import timeout_rabbitmq if __name__ == '__main__': for i in range(20): r1 = timeout_rabbitmq.delay() ``` with a RabbitMQ instance in the background. - Run run.py. - Cut the connection between the worker and the broker (by Ctrl C/docker kill the docker container of the RabbitMQ or by having a PRECONDITION_FAILED cuased by a timeout on the RabbitMQ, for example). - Restart the RabbitMQ. - When the connection is established, cut a second time the connection between the worker and the broker. - Restart the RabbitMQ. - The worker crashed.

# Expected Behavior The worker must stay up after the second reconnection and not crash. # Actual Behavior The worker crashed. I dug into the code and found that in the function iterate_file_descriptors_safely in concurrency/asynpool.py L.211, some of the fd transformed into NoneType, resulting in an AttributeError not captured by the except L.216 (https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/main/celery/concurrency/asynpool.py#L211). By adding the AttributeError to the except, the expected behavior is observed. ```python for fd in fds_iter: # Handle using the correct arguments to the hub method hub_args, hub_kwargs = _meta_fd_argument_maker(), kwargs try: # Call the hub method hub_method(fd, *hub_args, **hub_kwargs) except (OSError, FileNotFoundError, AttributeError): logger.warning( "Encountered OSError when accessing fd %s ", fd, exc_info=True) stale_fds.append(fd) # take note of stale fd ``` ``` -------------- celery@eloi-Latitude-5420 v5.5.0b3 (immunity) --- ***** ----- -- ******* ---- Linux-6.8.0-41-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 2024-09-10 09:56:05 - *** --- * --- - ** ---------- [config] - ** ---------- .> app: src:0x7a777d56ae70 - ** ---------- .> transport: amqp://guest:**@localhost:5672// - ** ---------- .> results: disabled:// - *** --- * --- .> concurrency: 8 (prefork) -- ******* ---- .> task events: ON --- ***** ----- -------------- [queues] .> celery exchange=celery(direct) key=celery [tasks] . src.tasks.fail_on_purpose . src.tasks.looping . src.tasks.test . src.tasks.timeout_rabbitmq [2024-09-10 09:56:05,971: INFO/MainProcess] Connected to amqp://guest:**@127.0.0.1:5672// [2024-09-10 09:56:05,979: INFO/MainProcess] mingle: searching for neighbors [2024-09-10 09:56:07,004: INFO/MainProcess] mingle: all alone [2024-09-10 09:56:07,021: INFO/MainProcess] celery@eloi-Latitude-5420 ready.
